text.p: The Turkish lira fell to 90,820 against the dollar on Monday from 90,420 at Friday's close amid continuing dollar demand by banks and also due to central bank's higher dollar rate for banks' forex transfers, bankers said.
The Turkish central bank set its dollar rate for banks' compulsory currency transfers at 90,650 lira at the opening, up from 90,350 at Friday's close.
Bankers said expectations of higher inflation in the last quarter continued to fuel demand for the U.S. currency despite persistent cash squeeze.

They said cash demand remained strong as banks repaid the central bank a total of 45.2 trillion lira borrowed via previous repo auctions and 24 trillion lira borrowed overnight at 75 percent on Friday.

The central bank injected a total of 50.65 trillion lira -- 23.45 trillion lira by buying seven-day repos at an average annual rate of 74.31 percent in an open market auction and 27.2 trillion lira by overnight lending at 75 percent on the interbank.
Overnight money also traded at 74.75 percent in the day.
T-bill yields firmed by around one point ahead of the Treasury's announcement of this week t-bill auction on cash shortage.

The average yield on the most heavily traded March 26 paper firmed to 126.68 percent from 125.64 on Friday. The second most active March 12 paper yielded 126.21 percent, up from 124.82 percent Friday average.
The Treasury will auction 196-day t-bills on Tuesday with Wednesday value date when 127.5 trillion lira will be cashed in from maturing t-bills. -- Istanbul Newsroom, +90-212-275 0875
